scope: Static ABI review for an explicit isolated-display scheduling experiment; no inferior-call performed by this script

preferred_api.name: Original delay API, dly_tsk-like
preferred_api.effect: Original API adds1 and stores60001 in TCB+0x4c, changes wait_type to2, then calls original scheduler0x06498810
preferred_api.clock: Original timer0 LOAD0x6978 at configured27MHz produces1ms callbacks; nominal60001ticks about60.001seconds of guest virtual time
preferred_api.bounds: No explicit upper-limit validation found;60000 does not wrap the argument+1 arithmetic
checks: Current task via0x06508492 must be nonnull
0x08ab4e68 must equal0 together with a repeated interrupt-context check
preferred_api.runtime_precedent: menu-smp/results/pulse-timer-boot proved original0x066c23e8(1) returned after repeated ticks

inferior_call_contract.do_not_call_from: Final snapshot PC0x18/CPSR IRQ; that is an interrupt sampling point, not the task context
inferior_call_contract.preserve: Full original CPU register context including CPSR and available VFP state; preserve original task SP for call
inferior_call_contract.call: Set r0=60000, LR=an independent executable scratch-return address|1, PC=0x066c23e8 with original Thumb task CPSR. Keep original task stack and do not patch task fields.
inferior_call_contract.return: A separate code breakpoint at scratch-return verifies API return; only then restore saved original context and continue original busy loop if desired
inferior_call_contract.during_wait: Other tasks may execute. Do not restore the saved task66 register context onto a different running task. A run ended before return remains an interrupted isolated scheduling experiment.
limits: Delayingtask66 does not complete coprocessor boot or release locks it may own.
Any further UI wait on its state/locks is real evidence and must not be cleared by hand.
60second argument is guest virtual time, not a guaranteed wall-clock timeout; retain outer process/time bounds.
